{He} left the academy with a scholar's learning and no money, and has paid for {his} books with Quests ever since.
older: {He} has practised the craft for twenty years, and treats every new spell as a debt to be paid.
{He} keeps notebooks of every spell {he} has cast in twenty years, and reads the early ones with some embarrassment.
{He} has buried two apprentices who were cleverer than {he} was, and teaches caution now before anything else.

young: {He} learned herb-lore from a village wise-woman, and set {his} first bone at twelve.
{He} was taught in a temple infirmary, and left it for the road when {he} saw how many of the wounded never reached one.
{He} learned to stitch a wound on {his} own brothers, who gave {him} more practice than {he} ever wanted.
middle: {He} has patched up soldiers, miners and fools for ten years, and lost fewer of them than anyone expected.
{He} has worked through a plague summer and a hard siege, and is surprised by very little that a body can do.
{He} has followed Parties into the wild for the better part of ten years, and can set a bone by firelight.
older: {He} has sat at more sickbeds than {he} can count, and still believes every patient can be saved.
{He} has trained a generation of village midwives and bonesetters, and hears {his} methods, garbled, wherever {he} goes.
{His} hands have grown less steady with the years, but {his} judgement of a wound has only grown sharper.

scarred: {He} carries the scars of a Quest {he} will not talk about.
A blade opened {his} face on a Quest in the fells, and the scar still whitens when {he} is angry.
{His} forearms are laced with old scars, and {he} tells a different story for each one to anyone who asks.
lame: An old Injury left {him} lame, and {he} hates to be helped on the stairs.
{He} has walked with a stick since a fall on a Quest, and can still keep pace with most Parties, if not for long.
A leg badly set after an Injury left {him} with a limp that worsens in the cold and the wet.
one-eyed: {He} lost an eye on a Quest, and watches twice as hard with the one that is left.
An Injury took one of {his} eyes, and {he} keeps anyone {he} does not trust on {his} good side.
{He} has misjudged distances since losing the eye, and makes up for it by getting closer than most would dare.
short-winded: {He} has been short of breath since a bad Injury, and resents every hill between {him} and a Quest.
A crushed chest on a Quest left {him} short of breath, and {he} has learned to do everything in short, hard bursts.
{He} breathed too much smoke on a Quest gone wrong, and {his} rasping breath gives {him} away in any quiet place.

young: {He} is young, and means to make a name before anyone thinks to ask {his} age.
{He} is still learning which risks are worth taking, and has so far been lucky with the ones that were not.
{He} takes every Quest as a chance to be noticed, and has not yet learned to count the cost first.
middle: {He} has seen enough Quests to be careful, and enough to know that care is not always enough.
{He} is past the recklessness of youth and not yet slowed by caution, which suits most Parties well.
{He} knows {his} own limits now, and is honest about them, which makes {him} a steadier Hero than many.
older: {He} has outlasted most of the Heroes {he} started with, and means to outlast the rest.
{He} is slower than {he} was, and wiser for it, and the young Heroes would do well to listen to {him}.
{He} knows every trick of the road by now, and meets each new Quest with the respect the old ones taught {him}.
